title: data-finops
text: data-finops allocates a cloud bill to the Query Executions, dbt Model Executions and Workload Runs that caused it. The bill stays authoritative: every amount it allocates reconciles to a Billing Line, and every estimate says how confident it is. It runs on your machine. It can also run as a Deployment in your own AWS account, which collects the bill and the workload metadata one time each day. See Deployment architecture. To see it on a real bill, look at the Public Demo: the dashboard of a real Deployment. Its workload is simulated, but its Athena charges are real and reconciled to the bill. To see how it compares with the cost tools of AWS, read Compared with AWS's cost tools. This documentation is for people who run data-finops. It has four parts: Tutorials: learn data-finops: allocate a bill, step by step. How-to guides: do one task, for example load a bill or serve the API. Reference: look up commands, routes, data contracts and terms. Explanation: understand why data-finops works the way it does. To work on data-finops itself, start at Contribute to data-finops.

title: Tutorials
text: A tutorial takes you through data-finops from start to finish on sample data. Follow it in order.

title: Your first allocation
headings: 1. Load the bill and the workload
4. Follow $6.00 to its Query Execution, Model Execution and Workload Runs
5. A Model Execution with no linked Query Execution gets nothing
text: In this tutorial we load a small bill and the metadata of the workload that ran against it. Then we allocate the bill and follow $10.00 of cost to the Query Execution, dbt Model Execution and Airflow Workload Runs that used it. It takes about five minutes and does not use a cloud account. The inputs are synthetic test fixtures, not real AWS billing records or provider prices. On each change to data-finops, a test runs each command in steps 1 to 8. The test also checks each output that is marked as checked. Thus what you see in these steps is what you will see. Before you start Before you start, install Python 3.12 and uv. Also get a source checkout, because the tutorial reads the fixtures in fixtures/: git clone https://github.com/apmalong/data-finops.git cd data-finops uv sync --extra api --frozen Then activate the environment, so that data-finops is on your path: source .venv/bin/activate, or .venv\Scripts\activate on Windows. You can instead start each command below with uv run. 1. Load the bill and the workload We load four kinds of input into one database file, demo.sqlite: one FOCUS Export Snapshot with two Billing Lines, $6.00 of Athena and $4.00 of S3 the Athena query history the Airflow and dbt OpenLineage events the dbt artifacts data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10.json --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/query-executions.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/link-outcomes.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/link-outcomes-restated.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest openlineage fixtures/openlineage/events.json --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/manifest.json --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/run_results.json --db demo.sqlite Each command says what it stored. The last Athena file restates one Query Execution, so it is counted as a changed copy. 2. Calculate data-finops calculate --db demo.sqlite The Calculation Run splits every Billing Line into Allocations and stores them as the current Allocation Snapshot. It prints one line per Snapshot Scope: the account, the Billing Period and the source, then the Calculation Run. 3. See where the bill went We serve the dashboard and the API over the database, and ask the API for the Cost Summary: data-finops serve --db demo.sqlite curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/costs/summary?cost_basis=BilledCost' serve does not stop, so run curl in a second terminal. Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ in a browser. The dashboard shows the same answer: The BilledCost total is 10.00 USD, and the Reconciliation Delta is 0.00: every cent of the bill is in exactly one Allocation. Under the title are the Calculation Run, when it ran, and the policy version it used. 4. Follow $6.00 to its Query Execution, Model Execution and Workload Runs Direct, metered estimate, Coverage 1: 6.00. It is an estimate, so it is always shown with its Confidence and Coverage. We ask which Allocation it is, and what it rolls up to: curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/allocations?billing_account_id=123456789012&billing_period=2026-10-01&source=aws-data-exports:FOCUS_1_2_AWS&cost_basis=BilledCost&category=direct' curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/rollups?billing_account_id=123456789012&billing_period=2026-10-01&source=aws-data-exports:FOCUS_1_2_AWS&level=model_execution' The whole $6.00 Athena line goes to Query Execution q-001. The line bills exactly the Billable Usage of the known Query Executions in its billing scope. Thus Coverage is 1, and q-001 gets the line by its Billable Usage. In the dashboard, click Direct to open its Cost Explanation: It reads in order: the Billing Line as exported, the Allocation, the Evidence nearest first, and the Roll-ups. Model Execution model.demo.orders has $6.00, and so do the dbt Workload Run and the Airflow Workload Runs above it. A Roll-up is a sum of Allocations, never a further Allocation. 5. A Model Execution with no linked Query Execution gets nothing We ask for the lineage of the dbt run, 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002: curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/lineage?run_id=00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002' Only q-004 claims model.demo.customers, and its reports disagree, so its Link Outcome is ambiguous. With no Identity Link, nothing is invented for that Model Execution: it has no Roll-up. The dashboard shows the same under Workload Runs: 6. The $4.00 S3 line stays Unallocated In the Cost Summary from step 3, "unallocated":[{"reason":"ineligible","amount":"4.00"}]. No policy allocates S3 storage yet, so its $4.00 stays Unallocated, named with its reason, and is never spread over the Query Executions. The dashboard shows it in the highlight color. 7. Load everything again: nothing changes data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10.json --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/query-executions.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/link-outcomes.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/link-outcomes-restated.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest openlineage fixtures/openlineage/events.json --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/manifest.json --db demo.sqlite data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/run_results.json --db demo.sqlite data-finops calculate --db demo.sqlite data-finops recognizes each input as an input that is already stored. The calculation replays the same Calculation Run. The dashboard still shows $10.00. If you load the same inputs two times, data-finops never counts a cost two times. 8. The provider restates the bill Providers republish a month when charges change. Here October is republished with $5.00 of S3, as aws-focus-123456789012-2026-10-v2: data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10-restated.json --db demo.sqlite data-finops calculate --db demo.sqlite curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/costs/summary?cost_basis=BilledCost' The bill is now $11.00 and the new Calculation Run is current. data-finops keeps the previous Calculation Run and does not overwrite it. Ask for /v1/provenance?calculation_run_id= with the ID of the first run. The answer has "is_current": false, and superseded_by names the new run. What we did We loaded a bill and the metadata of the workload behind it. Then we allocated each Billing Line. After that, we saw these results: $6.00 went through a Query Execution to its Model Execution and Workload Runs. A Model Execution with no Evidence got nothing. $4.00 stayed Unallocated, with its reason. A restated bill made a new Allocation Snapshot and kept the old one. To try the whole thing in one command, data-finops demo loads every fixture into a temporary database, calculates, and serves the dashboard until you press Ctrl+C.

title: How-to guides
text: A how-to guide gets one task done. It assumes you know what you want and have data-finops installed.

title: Install data-finops
headings: Install with the API and dashboard
text: This guide installs the data-finops command from a source checkout. Nothing is released yet, so there is no package on PyPI to install. Not run on this page: it changes your machine. What you must have Python 3.12 or later. uv, which installs the pinned dependencies. git, to clone the repository. Install with the API and dashboard git clone https://github.com/apmalong/data-finops.git cd data-finops uv sync --extra api --frozen uv run data-finops --help The api extra adds FastAPI and uvicorn. serve and demo require them to run the API, the dashboard and the OpenLineage receiver. --frozen installs exactly the versions in uv.lock. Install without the extra uv sync --frozen The base package can ingest and calculate. serve and demo exit with 2 and say that the API requires the api extra. demo checks this before it writes anything. Install it with uv sync --extra api --frozen. Try it with the demo uv run data-finops demo demo loads the hand-written fixtures into a temporary database file, runs a Calculation Run and serves on loopback at http://127.0.0.1:8000/. It reads the repository's fixtures/ directory, so it requires a source checkout: an installed package does not include the fixtures. The database file is removed when demo stops. Next, follow the tutorial Your first allocation, which runs the same steps one at a time.

title: Ingest a FOCUS export
headings: Load an Export Snapshot from a JSON file
Load an AWS Data Exports Delivery
text: This guide loads an Export Snapshot into a database file: all the Billing Lines of one billing account, Billing Period and source, as the provider published them. It comes from a FOCUS JSON file or from an AWS Data Exports Delivery. Load an Export Snapshot from a JSON file data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10.json --db finops.sqlite The database file is created if it does not exist. The line gives the outcome, then the Export Snapshot's ID: new: it is stored, and it is now the current Export Snapshot of its Snapshot Scope. superseded: it is stored as a Superseded Snapshot, because a later publication of the same Snapshot Scope is current. replay: nothing is stored, because the same content is already there. Load it again safely data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10.json --db finops.sqlite A replay stores nothing, so you can run an ingest again and get no copies. Which Export Snapshot is current depends on the provider's publication time, never on the order you load them in (ADR 0020). Load an AWS Data Exports Delivery AWS Data Exports writes each Delivery as a manifest, <export>-Manifest.json, and its data files. Download both, then give ingest focus the manifest: data-finops ingest focus <download-dir>/<export>-Manifest.json --data-dir <data-files-dir> --db finops.sqlite Not run on this page: it requires a Delivery downloaded from AWS. --data-dir names where the data files were downloaded. Leave it out when they are beside the manifest. The publication time comes from the manifest, never from file times or the time you load it. Collect Deliveries on a schedule A Collection Run finds and loads Deliveries itself. Run one from your machine with data-finops collect, as Send workload metadata to the Inbox shows. A Deployment runs one every day. Set the export to create new files when it updates a period, in the Data Exports console. Each Delivery then has a folder of its own, and its publication time comes from that folder. A Collection Run refuses an export that overwrites its files, and shows a warning. For the billing_lookback_periods most recent Billing Periods (default 2, at most 24), a Collection Run does these steps: It finds each Delivery whose two manifests are written. A Delivery that AWS still writes stays for a later run. A Delivery that a run took before is never downloaded again. It loads each Delivery that is newer than the current Export Snapshot of its Snapshot Scope, oldest first. Thus the newest becomes current, and the others are kept as Superseded Snapshots. It downloads only the data files that the manifest lists, and only from the folder of that Delivery in the export. If a manifest names a different file, data-finops rejects the manifest and does not read that file. Before it downloads a file of a Delivery, it refuses the Delivery if its data files are more than 8 GiB together. It also refuses each data file over 2 GiB. A refused Delivery is named by its folder and the reason, and the run exits with 1. If the ingest is refused Nothing is stored, and the command exits with 2: The file is not a FOCUS Export Snapshot, or the Delivery is not usable. The message names the file, never its content. An Export Snapshot with the same ID is already stored with other content. Stored Export Snapshots never change. See Exit codes and environment. Next, calculate the Allocations.

title: Ingest Athena query history
text: Athena's query history gives the Query Executions behind an Athena bill: how much each one scanned and, through its Trusted Query Comment, which Model Execution issued it. This guide fetches the history from AWS and loads it. Fetch the history from AWS List the Query Execution IDs of a workgroup, then fetch them with BatchGetQueryExecution, which takes at most 50 IDs per call: aws athena list-query-executions --work-group <workgroup> --max-items 50 --output json aws athena batch-get-query-execution --query-execution-ids <id> <id> … --output json > query-executions.json Not run on this page: it requires AWS credentials and an Athena workgroup. Save the response as it is. In Windows PowerShell 5.1, > saves a file as UTF-16, which data-finops cannot read, so the Windows version saves it through cmd. data-finops reads the plain BatchGetQueryExecution response, up to 512 MiB per file. Load it The response does not say which account and Region it came from, so give them alongside it: data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/query-executions.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --db finops.sqlite duplicates: Query Executions already stored with the same content. changed copies: a Query Execution already stored, reported again with different content. Both are kept, and the Query Execution gets a flag for observations that conflict. rejected: an entry that fails validation. It is named by its position and the reason, never by its content. The rest is stored, and the command exits with 1. A file that is not a BatchGetQueryExecution response prints athena: rejected: with the reason. Nothing from it is stored, and the command exits with 1. Load history that overlaps Fetches often overlap. If you load the same history again, nothing new is stored: data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/query-executions.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --db finops.sqlite What is kept Only allowlisted metadata is stored: identity, workgroup, statement type, catalog and database, state, times, error category and type, numeric statistics and engine version. Query text, execution parameters and error messages are dropped. From the Trusted Query Comment, only its invocation_id and node_id are kept. To send that comment, see Ingest dbt artifacts. Collect it on a schedule A Collection Run fetches the history itself, for the workgroups its settings name. Run one from your machine with data-finops collect, as Send workload metadata to the Inbox shows. A Deployment runs one every day. For each workgroup, the run does these steps: It lists the Query Execution IDs of the workgroup, 50 on each page, in max_history_pages pages at most (default 200, at most 1,000). It fetches only the Query Executions that are not stored yet, 50 at a time. It stores the finished Query Executions, with only the metadata listed above. A Query Execution that is still queued or in progress stays for a later run. Athena keeps 45 days of query history. A Collection Run shows a warning when it can have lost some history: The page cap was reached, so older Query Executions were not listed. Raise max_history_pages. None of the Query Executions already stored for the workgroup is still in Athena's history. The Query Executions that ran in the gap can have expired before a run read them. Then Coverage is below 1. A Query Execution whose entry is rejected is named by its workgroup and ID, never its content. Throttled calls are retried, at most 5 attempts in all. After that the source fails, and the run exits with 2.

title: Ingest dbt artifacts
headings: Load the manifest and the run results
Let Query Executions name their Model Execution
text: A dbt invocation writes manifest.json and run_results.json to its target/ directory. The manifest gives the dbt Nodes, and the run results give the Model Executions. This guide loads both. Load the manifest and the run results Load each artifact with its own command, in either order: data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/manifest.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/run_results.json --db finops.sqlite Each line names the dbt invocation the artifact belongs to. Copy the artifacts out of target/ after each invocation, because the next one overwrites them. Load them again data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/manifest.json --db finops.sqlite An artifact already stored with the same content stores nothing. Another artifact of the same kind for the same invocation prints changed_copy, and is kept beside the first. If an artifact is rejected A file that is not a dbt manifest or run results prints dbt: rejected: with the reason, such as not a dbt artifact. Nothing from it is stored, and the command exits with 1. Let Query Executions name their Model Execution dbt artifacts do not name the Athena Query Executions a Model Execution issued. To link them, configure dbt to send a Trusted Query Comment with the invocation_id and node_id of each dbt Node it runs. dbt's default query comment has no invocation_id. The configuration is in the reference workload's README. Then ingest the Athena history.

title: Receive OpenLineage events
headings: Point an OpenLineage client at it
text: OpenLineage RunEvents tell data-finops about Workload Runs: an Airflow DAG run, the dbt run inside it, and how they nest. This guide loads them from a file, then receives them over HTTP. Load events from a file The file holds a JSON array of events, or one event per line (JSON Lines): data-finops ingest openlineage fixtures/openlineage/events.json --db finops.sqlite duplicates: events already stored with the same content. If you load the file again, nothing is stored. changed copies: an event already stored, reported again with different content. Both are kept. unsupported: a JobEvent or DatasetEvent, which data-finops does not read. These do not change the exit code. rejected: an event that is not a valid RunEvent. The rest of the file is stored, and the command exits with 1. Each unsupported or rejected event is named by its position and the reason, never by its content. For example: A file over 512 MiB is rejected whole, before it is read. Its line has the position 0: Receive events over HTTP serve also runs the receiver, at POST /api/v1/lineage, the default endpoint of OpenLineage's HTTP transport. Each request carries one event: data-finops serve --db finops.sqlite curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @fixtures/openlineage/one-event.json http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/lineage serve does not stop, so send events from a second terminal. The receiver screens each event exactly as it screens one item of a file: 201 with the counts above when the event is stored, or was already there. 202 for an unsupported event, which is not stored. 400 for a rejected event, with the reason. 413 for a body over the 1 MiB event cap. It is refused before it is read in full. 415 for a compressed body. Send each event uncompressed. A received event changes no Allocation until the next calculate. Point an OpenLineage client at it For an OpenLineage client that reads its settings from the environment, such as the Python client that Airflow and dbt use: export OPENLINEAGE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 export OPENLINEAGE_ENDPOINT=api/v1/lineage Not run on this page: it configures a client outside data-finops. To receive events from another machine, serve requires a token, which the client sends as its API key. See Serve with a token.

title: Send workload metadata to the Inbox
text: A Deployment does not receive OpenLineage events or dbt artifacts over HTTP. Producers write files to its Inbox, a prefix in the Deployment's bucket, and the next Collection Run pulls them (ADR 0027). This guide writes both kinds of file, then runs a Collection Run from your machine with data-finops collect. Not run on this page. These commands use your own AWS profile and a real bucket. In each command, replace example-deployment-bucket with your Deployment's bucket. What goes where inbox/openlineage/: OpenLineage event files, one event per file or JSON Lines. Each event is capped at 1 MiB, as on every other path. inbox/dbt/<invocation>/: one dbt invocation's manifest.json and run_results.json. A folder is collected when both files are in it. Until then, each Collection Run shows the warning <folder>/: waiting for <files>. Every file is capped at 512 MiB. A larger file is rejected by its key and never downloaded. Give the producer access The identity that writes requires s3:PutObject on inbox/*. If kmsKeyArn is set, it also requires kms:GenerateDataKey on that key. The stack outputs producerPolicyArn, a managed policy that grants these permissions and no others. Attach it to the role your Airflow or dbt runs as, for example: aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name <producer role> --policy-arn <producerPolicyArn> --profile <admin profile> The producer cannot read, list or delete what is in the Inbox. The bucket is the bucket output. pulumi stack output lists both outputs. See Deploy to AWS. Write OpenLineage events Have the OpenLineage client write events to local files with its file transport, for example in openlineage.yml: The file transport writes one file per event, each a single line of JSON, which data-finops reads as JSON Lines. Leave debug_mode off: it writes indented JSON that data-finops refuses. After the run, copy the files to the Inbox: aws s3 sync lineage/ s3://example-deployment-bucket/inbox/openlineage/ The file transport can also write to an s3:// path directly through fsspec, which requires the s3fs package installed beside the client. That set-up has not been verified with data-finops. Write dbt artifacts After each dbt run or dbt build, copy the two artifacts into a folder named after the invocation. You choose the folder name. data-finops reads the invocation from the files: aws s3 cp target/manifest.json s3://example-deployment-bucket/inbox/dbt/inv-001/manifest.json aws s3 cp target/run_results.json s3://example-deployment-bucket/inbox/dbt/inv-001/run_results.json Collect from your machine A Deployment runs a Collection Run every day, and its collector can be invoked to run one now (Deploy to AWS). To run one from your own machine instead, read-only against AWS, install the aws extra and write a settings file, for example collect.toml: uv sync --extra aws --frozen account_id and workgroups name the Athena workgroups. The run also collects the query history of these workgroups. See Ingest Athena query history. The three export_ settings name the FOCUS export, as it is configured in Data Exports. See Ingest a FOCUS export. profile and inbox_retention_days are optional. inbox_retention_days is the number of days after which S3 expires an Inbox object. The run uses it to warn before an object that it did not collect expires. data-finops refuses an unknown setting. Thus a typo never fails silently. Then collect into a database: data-finops collect --db finops.sqlite --config collect.toml collect prints one line of JSON: the summary of the Collection Run. For each source, the summary gives the number of stored items, the number of duplicates and the rejected items. Then it gives the warnings and the Calculation Runs that it started. Each rejected item follows on its own line, by key. For one event, the line also gives the position of the event in the file: An OpenLineage JobEvent or DatasetEvent, which data-finops does not read, is listed under warnings by key and position. It does not change the exit code. A dbt folder that does not have both of its files yet is also in that list, until the file arrives. A file that was collected is never fetched again, unless a producer overwrites it with new content. A rejected file is not retried. In a Deployment, Inbox objects expire after inboxRetentionDays (default 30), and the collector gets this setting. In its last 7 days, an object that was not collected is listed under warnings, with its key, its age and the days left. With a retention shorter than 7 days, each such object is listed: To keep the data, correct a rejected file and write it to the Inbox again. For a dbt folder, send the file that it waits for. Do this before the object expires. The exit code is 0, 1 when something was rejected, or 2 when a source could not be read. See Exit codes and environment.

title: Calculate Allocations
headings: When there is nothing to calculate
text: This guide runs a Calculation Run. It splits every Billing Line of the current Export Snapshots into Allocations, and stores them as the current Allocation Snapshot of each Snapshot Scope. Load the inputs first A Calculation Run reads only what is stored when it starts. Load the Export Snapshot and the workload's Athena history, OpenLineage events and dbt artifacts first: data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/query-executions.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --db finops.sqlite data-finops ingest openlineage fixtures/openlineage/events.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/manifest.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/run_results.json --db finops.sqlite The how-to guides for FOCUS, Athena, OpenLineage and dbt explain each input. Run the calculation data-finops calculate --db finops.sqlite It prints one line for each Snapshot Scope: the billing account, the Billing Period, the source, the outcome and the Calculation Run's ID. new means a new Allocation Snapshot is stored and current. Run it again data-finops calculate --db finops.sqlite With the same inputs and the same Allocation Policy, nothing new is stored, and the line names the current Calculation Run. Load new inputs and calculate again to change the Allocations. An event the HTTP receiver takes in changes no Allocation until the next calculate. When there is nothing to calculate A database file with no Export Snapshot prints calculate: no Export Snapshot to calculate and exits with 0. A --db path with no database file there exits with 2. Next, read a Cost Explanation, or handle a restated export.

title: Configure Cost Dimensions
headings: Read the totals of each value
text: A Cost Dimension groups cost by an attribute that your organization selects, for example a team or a tenant. You declare each dimension and where its value comes from in one TOML file. Each Calculation Run then records the value and its source on each Allocation. This guide writes the file, sends the values from dbt, calculates with the file and reads the totals of each value. The decision is ADR 0031, and the rules are in spec 09. A dimension is a view of the Allocations. It does not change how a Billing Line is split. Its value is a claim: it tells you what a query comment, a tag or a map says. It is never Evidence for an Identity Link. Write the file This guide uses fixtures/docs/cost-dimensions.toml: [dimensions.team] sources = ["query_comment.team", "workgroup_map"] workgroup_map = { "demo" = "analytics" } [dimensions.environment] sources = ["query_comment.target_name"] Each table under dimensions is one dimension. Its sources are tried in order, and the first source that gives a value wins. There are three kinds of source: query_comment.<key>: a key in the JSON comment on the first line of the query, the same comment that holds the Trusted Query Comment. openlineage_tag.<key>: a tag in the OpenLineage tags facets (of the run and of its job) of the Workload Run of the query's dbt invocation. The tags of that run come first, then the tags of its parents, up to the root run. If one run has two values for the key, that run is skipped, and its parents are tried. workgroup_map: the Athena workgroup of the query, through the map that the dimension gives. For an amount with no query, it is the workgroup of the Billing Line. The rules: A file has 8 dimensions at most, and its query_comment sources name 16 keys at most. Ingest keeps only the comment keys that the file names. A value longer than 128 characters is removed, and the ingest result counts it as a dropped claim. An unknown key or source refuses the file. The error names the file and the fault, never a value. Add sensitive = true to a dimension to keep its values out of the minimal Cost Explanation and out of the public demo. The full API still shows them. Send the values from dbt dbt sends a comment on the first line of each query that it runs. Make that comment JSON, with the Trusted Query Comment's invocation_id and node_id, and with each key that your dimensions read. Put this macro in macros/data_finops_query_comment.sql of your dbt project: {% macro data_finops_query_comment(node) -%} {%- set comment = { "app": "dbt", "dbt_version": dbt_version, "invocation_id": invocation_id, "node_id": node.unique_id if node is not none else none, "target_name": target.name, "team": node.config.meta.get("team") if node is not none else none, } -%} {{- return(tojson(comment)) -}} {%- endmacro %} Then select it in dbt_project.yml. The comment must be at the start of the query, so do not append it: query-comment: comment: "{{ data_finops_query_comment(node) }}" append: false This macro reads the team from each model's meta, for example {{ config(meta={"team": "finance"}) }}. You can also read a value from an environment variable that your orchestrator sets, with env_var("TEAM", ""). The reference workload uses the same macro without team: see its README. The macro writes the same comment for each query of a model, so each query of the model gets the same claims. Ingest with the file Give the same file to ingest athena and to calculate. Ingest keeps the claims, and the Calculation Run resolves them: data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/query-executions.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --dimensions fixtures/docs/cost-dimensions.toml --db finops.sqlite data-finops calculate --dimensions fixtures/docs/cost-dimensions.toml --db finops.sqlite data-finops serve --db finops.sqlite serve does not stop, so run the next command in a second terminal. The configuration applies only from now on: A comment key that you add later applies only to the queries that are ingested after it. The query text is not kept, so the key cannot be read again from stored queries. A changed file does not change a stored Allocation Snapshot, and it does not start a new snapshot by itself. It applies at the next snapshot that new inputs make. Each snapshot records the SHA-256 of the file that it used. Read the totals of each value Ask for the Roll-ups of one dimension: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/rollups/dimensions/team Read it in this order: totals is the total of the Allocation Snapshot for each currency and Cost Basis: $10.00 BilledCost. The values always add up to it, so you do not have to add them. analytics has $6.00. The fixture's comments have no team key, so the second source gave the value: the query ran in the demo workgroup, which the map gives to analytics. The value null is unassigned: $4.00. It is the S3 line, which has no query and no workgroup. Unassigned cost stays visible. It is never spread among the other values. A dimension that no Allocation of the snapshot has gives 404. The dashboard shows the same totals in its Cost Dimensions section, with a list to select the dimension. In a Deployment Set the stack's costDimensions setting to the path of your file, then run pulumi up. The stack uploads the file to config/cost-dimensions.toml in the Deployment's bucket, and only the collector can read it. The collector reads it at the start of each Collection Run. If it cannot read or use the file, the run stops, and the error names the key of the object, never its content. See Deployment settings. data-finops collect takes a --dimensions file, or the key of the object in its settings (cost_dimensions_key), but not both.

title: Handle a restated export
headings: Load the restated Export Snapshot and recalculate
Check that the new Calculation Run is current
An older Export Snapshot loaded late
text: A provider can publish a Billing Period again with changed Billing Lines. This guide loads the restated Export Snapshot and recalculates. Nothing earlier is overwritten. Start from a calculated bill data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops calculate --db finops.sqlite data-finops serve --db finops.sqlite serve does not stop, so run the other commands in a second terminal. Load the restated Export Snapshot and recalculate data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10-restated.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops calculate --db finops.sqlite The restated Export Snapshot is published later, so it is now current. The earlier one becomes a Superseded Snapshot and is kept. A restatement replaces the whole Export Snapshot, never single Billing Lines (ADR 0015). Check that the new Calculation Run is current Set CALCULATION_RUN_ID to the ID the last calculate printed: CALCULATION_RUN_ID=calc-<the ID calculate printed> curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/provenance?calculation_run_id=$CALCULATION_RUN_ID" Ask for the first Calculation Run's ID the same way: it answers "is_current":false, and superseded_by names the new run. Its Allocation Snapshot is kept as history. An older Export Snapshot loaded late Exports can arrive out of order. Into a new database file, load the restated Export Snapshot first, then the earlier one: data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10-restated.json --db late.sqlite data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10.json --db late.sqlite The earlier publication is stored as a Superseded Snapshot, and the latest publication stays current, in any load order (ADR 0020). If you load an Export Snapshot that is already stored, the command prints replay and stores nothing.

title: Read a Cost Explanation
headings: Show less of the Billing Line
text: A Cost Explanation shows why one Allocation got its amount: the Billing Line it came from, the Allocation, its Evidence and the Roll-ups it adds to. This guide finds an Allocation through the API and reads its Cost Explanation (spec 06). Calculate and serve Load a bill and its workload, then calculate: data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops ingest athena fixtures/athena/query-executions.json --account-id 123456789012 --region us-east-1 --db finops.sqlite data-finops ingest openlineage fixtures/openlineage/events.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/manifest.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops ingest dbt fixtures/dbt/run_results.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops calculate --db finops.sqlite data-finops serve --db finops.sqlite serve does not stop, so run the other commands in a second terminal. Set CALCULATION_RUN_ID to the ID that calculate printed: CALCULATION_RUN_ID=calc-<the ID calculate printed> Find the Allocation List the Calculation Run's direct Allocations: curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/allocations?calculation_run_id=$CALCULATION_RUN_ID&cost_basis=BilledCost&category=direct" Each item's ref addresses one Allocation as <calculation_run_id>#<position>. This one gives $6.00 to Query Execution q-001. Read its Cost Explanation Ask for /v1/allocations/<ref>/explanation. Send the # as %23: curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/allocations/$CALCULATION_RUN_ID%230/explanation" Read it in order: billing_line: the Billing Line exactly as exported, every FOCUS column included. billing_line_detail says how much of it is shown: full here. allocation: its Allocation Category, method, Confidence, Coverage, Allocation Policy version and Calculation Run. The Evidence, each reference resolved: query_execution, then model_execution with its dbt Node, then workload_runs, nearest first. A Workload Run known only as another's parent or root shows "run":null. rollups: each Roll-up the Allocation adds to, in its currency and Cost Basis. For an Unallocated Allocation, unallocated_reason says why it is Unallocated, such as ineligible. The dashboard shows the same Cost Explanation when you click an Allocation. Show less of the Billing Line Tags and free-text names often carry team, customer or project names. If the readers of the API must not see them, serve a minimal Billing Line (ADR 0028): data-finops serve --db finops.sqlite --explanation-detail minimal Each Cost Explanation then shows "billing_line_detail":"minimal". Its Billing Line keeps the columns that data-finops uses in its calculations: the cost columns, accounts, periods, and charge category and class provider, service, SKU, region, ResourceId and SubAccountId quantities and units The line also keeps the raw provider values of these columns. Tags and each other column, for example ChargeDescription and the x_ columns of the provider, are left out. Amounts, Evidence and Roll-ups are the same at the two levels.

title: Serve with a token
headings: Serve with the token in the environment
text: serve runs the API, the dashboard and the OpenLineage receiver. On loopback, a token is optional. To serve on a different address, a token is necessary. This guide sets a token and serves with it (ADR 0024). Make a token A token is at least 16 characters. Make a long random one and keep it in a file only you can read: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))" > finops.token This page uses fixtures/docs/example.token, which holds the dummy token example-token-not-a-secret. Never use it for a real server. Serve with a token file data-finops ingest focus fixtures/focus/export-2026-10.json --db finops.sqlite data-finops serve --db finops.sqlite --token-file fixtures/docs/example.token curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat fixtures/docs/example.token)" http://127.0.0.1:8000/health $(cat …) puts the token in the header, but does not write it into the command. Thus with your own token, use $(cat finops.token). Now each route requires the header Authorization: Bearer <token>, also the dashboard and the API documentation. A request without it, or with a different token, gets 401: An OpenLineage client sends the token as its API key, for example in OPENLINEAGE_API_KEY. See Receive OpenLineage events. Serve with the token in the environment In place of --token-file, you can set DATA_FINOPS_TOKEN: export DATA_FINOPS_TOKEN="$(cat finops.token)" data-finops serve --db finops.sqlite Not run on this page: pages run with no DATA_FINOPS_* settings. Use the variable or a file, never both. With both, serve refuses to start: Serve off loopback To accept requests from other machines, give --host with a token: data-finops serve --db finops.sqlite --host 0.0.0.0 --token-file finops.token Without a token, serve refuses and exits with 2: Only a literal loopback address, such as 127.0.0.1 or ::1, counts as loopback. A name such as localhost also requires a token, because it can resolve to any address. The token travels in plain text over HTTP. Off loopback, put the server behind TLS. demo ignores any token. It always serves on loopback with every route open. The token is never logged, printed or stored. The rules are listed in Exit codes and environment.

title: Deploy the reference workload
headings: Run the workload and collect its outputs
text: The reference workload is a small Athena, dbt and Airflow pipeline in a real AWS account. It produces a real bill, real Athena history and real OpenLineage events, to check data-finops against more than the hand-written fixtures (ADR 0021). This guide deploys it with Pulumi, runs it and tears it down. The full steps are in the reference workload's README. Not run on this page. It creates resources in a real AWS account and costs real money. The owner approves every pulumi preview, pulumi up, workload run and pulumi destroy against a real account. What it deploys and costs The Pulumi program creates these resources in us-east-1: an S3 bucket, with public access blocked and encryption on a Glue database, reference_workload an Athena workgroup, data-finops-reference, that writes its results to the bucket as an option, an AWS Budget that sends alerts by email The costs are small. The tiny models cost a fraction of a cent per run, and the S3 and Glue costs are negligible. Two settings bound them: the workgroup's per-query scan cutoff, and the optional Budget. The Budget is account-wide, and it alerts when forecast or actual spend reaches its amount. Configure the stack Use a dedicated AWS profile with least privilege. From the repository root: cd examples/reference-workload uv sync export PULUMI_BACKEND_URL="file://$(cd ../.. && pwd)/.local/pulumi" export PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE="<choose one; needed for every later command>" pulumi stack init dev pulumi config set aws:profile <your profile> pulumi config set bytesScannedCutoffPerQuery 104857600 pulumi config set budgetMonthlyUsd <amount> pulumi config set budgetEmail <your email> PULUMI_BACKEND_URL keeps the Pulumi state in the git-ignored .local/pulumi. The program refuses any backend that is not file://. bytesScannedCutoffPerQuery is the maximum that an Athena query can scan, in bytes. The default is 100 MiB, and the least is 10 MiB. budgetMonthlyUsd and budgetEmail go together. Leave both unset for no Budget. pulumi stack init dev is necessary only the first time. Deploy pulumi preview pulumi up The stack's outputs are the bucket, the database and the workgroup. The runs of the workload require the bucket. Run the workload and collect its outputs The README gives the steps for dbt, run from WSL or Linux with dbt-ol, and for Airflow, run with Docker Compose. Their OpenLineage events land in the git-ignored .local/openlineage/. Before anything leaves your machine, anonymize the outputs with the secret described in Exit codes and environment: export DATA_FINOPS_ANON_SECRET="<long random value>" uv run python scripts/anonymize_focus_export.py <downloaded-export-dir> <output-dir> uv run python scripts/anonymize_workload_outputs.py <outputs-dir> <output-dir> Run these from the repository root. The output must be outside the repository or under .local/. The published sample is in fixtures/reference-workload/. Tear it down pulumi destroy This command removes the bucket with all its contents, the Glue database, the workgroup and the Budget. pulumi destroy does not remove these items: the local state in .local/pulumi and the outputs in .local/openlineage/ the WSL virtual environment, .venv-linux The reference workload was torn down on 2026-11-07 (issue #26). The record is in progress.md. Its stack configuration is kept, so the steps on this page can deploy it again: configure the stack, then deploy.

title: Deploy to AWS
headings: Check it with the policy pack
text: A Deployment runs data-finops in one AWS account (ADR 0026). It has a collector function that runs a Collection Run one time each day. It also has a read-only API behind an API Gateway HTTP API that IAM authorizes. This guide builds the functions' package, configures the Pulumi stack, checks it with the policy pack, deploys it and runs a first Collection Run. Deployment architecture explains what it creates and what it costs. Owner-run: not run on this page. Every command here reaches a real AWS account, and the deploy creates resources that cost money. Only the account owner runs pulumi preview, pulumi up and pulumi destroy against a real account. The owner can follow this page by hand, or run it as one wizard: deploy-and-verify.sh. The wizard does these things: It runs each step below. It checks what a destroy would keep. It can validate the IAM policies with IAM Access Analyzer. It runs a first Collection Run and reads its result. It can add the Public Demo. Then the wizard deploys the demo, writes the demo's dataset, runs the Simulated Orchestrator one time and opens demoUrl. It asks before each step that changes something. It masks account IDs, buckets, profiles and the URL of the API in all that it shows and records. From the root of the repository, run the wizard: bash infra/pulumi/aws/wizards/deploy-and-verify.sh On Windows, it requires Git Bash, not the bash of WSL. Its masked record is written to .local/. Before you start One AWS account holds the FOCUS export's bucket, the Athena workgroups and the Deployment. data-finops does not support the export or the history of a different account. The FOCUS export uses the "create new" delivery mode, as Ingest a FOCUS export describes. A Collection Run refuses an export that overwrites its files. An export encrypted with a KMS key is not supported yet. The database fits in a function's /tmp. The ephemeralStorageMb setting gives the collector, the API and the publisher 10,240 MB by default. The database and the Inbox file that a run collects share this space. An AWS profile for a dedicated deployer identity, created by the account owner. The stack never creates it. A draft least-privilege policy for it is iam/deployer-policy.draft.json. It is not validated. The wizard can check it with IAM Access Analyzer. If the policy does not have a permission, pulumi up shows an access error. The Pulumi CLI, version 3.272.0, and uv. A test checks the installed CLI is that release. Build the package Both functions run from one zip built from your checkout. From the repository root: cd infra/pulumi/aws uv sync --frozen uv run python -m deployment.package This command downloads the arm64 wheels from PyPI. Then it writes build/data-finops-lambda.zip, about 66 MB. The versions are the versions in uv.lock. pulumi up refuses to run without the zip. After each change to the checkout, build the zip again. A changed zip deploys each function again. Configure the stack Still in infra/pulumi/aws: mkdir -p ../../../.local/pulumi export PULUMI_BACKEND_URL="file://$(cd ../../.. && pwd)/.local/pulumi" export PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE="<choose one; needed for every later command>" pulumi stack init dev pulumi config set aws:profile <your deployer profile> pulumi config set aws:region <region> pulumi config set exportBucket <export bucket> pulumi config set exportName <export name> pulumi config set exportPrefix <export prefix> pulumi config set --path 'workgroups[0]' <workgroup> PULUMI_BACKEND_URL keeps the stack's state in the repository's git-ignored .local/pulumi, which must exist first. The program refuses any backend that is not file://. pulumi stack init dev is necessary only the first time. Leave out exportPrefix when the export has no S3 path prefix. Add a second workgroup as workgroups[1], and so on. Each other setting has a default. We recommend that you set two of them now: a Budget alert, and an alarm for when the collector fails. The Budget is for the whole account. It sends an alert about the forecast spend and the actual spend of the whole account, not only of the Deployment. pulumi config set budgetMonthlyUsd <amount> pulumi config set budgetEmail <your email> pulumi config set alarmEmail <your email> Once the stack is up, AWS emails alarmEmail a link to confirm its subscription to the alarm's topic. The alarm's emails start only after it is followed. Every setting, its default and its bounds are in Deployment settings. The stack checks them all before it declares anything. Check it with the policy pack The policy pack holds the mandatory rules of the Deployment: a private, encrypted, versioned bucket that accepts only TLS an API whose routes accept only IAM authorization, with rate limits functions with limits and logs least-privilege IAM no VPC and no database servers a Budget that sends alerts about forecast spend and actual spend The policy pack has its own environment: cd policy uv sync --frozen cd .. pulumi preview --policy-pack policy A violation fails the preview and names the policy and the resource. At a real preview, a policy document computed from other resources' ARNs is not known yet, so its checks are only advisory there. CI enforces them on every pull request, over the stack's mocked state. Deploy pulumi up --policy-pack policy Read the plan before you confirm it. The bucket and everything on it are kept when the stack is destroyed, unless deleteDataOnDestroy says otherwise: see Tear down a Deployment. Then list the stack's outputs: pulumi stack output Each output is described in Deployment settings. The next steps require collectorFunction and apiUrl. Run a first Collection Run The schedule starts the first run at its next time, 06:00 UTC by default. To run one now, invoke the collector. It ignores the event it is sent: aws lambda invoke --function-name <collectorFunction> --cli-read-timeout 900 --region <region> --profile <your profile> collector-result.json collector-result.json then holds the Collection Run's summary: for each source, what was stored, duplicated or rejected, any warnings, and the Calculation Run it started. The same summary is one line in the collector's log: aws logs tail /aws/lambda/<collectorFunction> --since 1h --region <region> --profile <your profile> A run that could not read a source, or that lost a write to a concurrent run, ends as an error. The schedule invokes the collector asynchronously, so Lambda retries a failed run up to twice. Each run starts again from the current database. If a run reads data that is already stored, nothing changes. To read what it collected, see Read a Deployment. To send it OpenLineage events and dbt artifacts, see Send workload metadata to the Inbox. Add the Public Demo (optional) The owner of data-finops runs the Public Demo in a Deployment. You do not need it to use data-finops. It adds a public site on CloudFront and an Athena workgroup with a generated dataset. It also adds a scheduled function that runs real queries in that workgroup. Those queries cost about $1 to $2 a month. The site publishes only the demo workgroup's lines, never the rest of the bill. In infra/pulumi/aws, turn the demo on and give it the demo's Cost Dimensions, then deploy again: pulumi config set publicDemo true pulumi config set costDimensions ../../../examples/public-demo/cost-dimensions.toml pulumi up --policy-pack policy examples/public-demo/cost-dimensions.toml groups cost by the team, the tenant and the Airflow run ID that the Simulated Orchestrator writes in each query comment. As in Airflow, the run ID is the scheduled time, so all the DAGs of one start have the same value. See Configure Cost Dimensions. The settings demoSchedule and demoScanCutoffBytes have defaults, which Deployment settings gives. The stack adds the demo workgroup to the workgroups whose history the collector reads. Write the demo dataset one time. The generator writes some hundred MB of Parquet, and takes some minutes: aws lambda invoke --function-name <demoGeneratorFunction> --cli-read-timeout 900 --region <region> --profile <your profile> generator-result.json If you invoke it again, it writes the same files. Then run the Simulated Orchestrator one time, so that you do not wait for its schedule. It runs the DAGs that are due now: aws lambda invoke --function-name <demoSimulatorFunction> --cli-read-timeout 900 --region <region> --profile <your profile> simulator-result.json The bill of these queries arrives in the FOCUS export some hours later. After the next Collection Run, the publisher writes the first Demo Snapshot. Then open demoUrl. Until the first snapshot, the demo shows nothing. To stop the demo, set publicDemo to false and run pulumi up. This deletes the demo's bucket and everything in it, because all of it can be made again. To stop only the queries, disable the simulator's schedule in EventBridge Scheduler.

title: Read a Deployment
headings: Open the dashboard on a local copy
text: A Deployment's API serves the same read endpoints as data-finops serve, from the database the last Collection Run wrote. It sits behind an API Gateway HTTP API. The API accepts only requests signed with AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) by an IAM principal that can call it. There is no token. This guide grants that access, calls the API, opens the dashboard on a local copy and switches the API off when necessary. Not run on this page. These commands reach a real Deployment with your own AWS credentials. Only an administrator can attach a policy. Only the owner runs the pulumi up of the kill switch. Grant a reader access The stack outputs readerPolicyArn, a managed policy that permits calls to the read routes of the API and nothing else. Attach it to the role or user that will read, for example: aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name <reader role> --policy-arn <readerPolicyArn> --profile <admin profile> The policy allows execute-api:Invoke on each read route, for example GET /v1/costs/summary. The stack also outputs consumerPolicyArn and operatorPolicyArn. At the moment, they allow the same read routes. Call the API A browser cannot sign SigV4, so use a client that can. awscurl signs with a named profile: uv tool install awscurl awscurl --service execute-api --region <region> --profile <reader profile> "<apiUrl>v1/costs/summary" <apiUrl> is the stack output, which ends in /. curl 7.75 and later can sign too, with --aws-sigv4 "aws:amz:<region>:execute-api" and the principal's keys. Every endpoint, parameter and response is in HTTP API, apart from POST /api/v1/lineage: a Deployment receives lineage through its Inbox, not over HTTP (Send workload metadata to the Inbox). An unsigned request, or one from a principal not allowed to invoke the route, gets 403 from AWS before data-finops sees it. The reader policy is one way to give this permission. A principal with broader permissions, for example an administrator, also has permission. Only the read routes under /v1/ are on the API. Any other path, /health included, gets 404 from AWS. More than apiRateLimit requests a second (default 10), or a burst of more than apiBurstLimit (default 20), gets 429. Before the first Collection Run there is no database yet, and every route answers 503. A Cost Explanation shows the minimal Billing Line by default: its tags, free-text names and provider extension columns are withheld, and billing_line_detail says minimal (ADR 0028). Set explanationDetail to full to show the whole line. See Read a Cost Explanation. Open the dashboard on a local copy The dashboard is not served by a Deployment. Download the database the last Collection Run wrote, then serve it on your own machine: aws s3 cp s3://<bucket>/database/data-finops.sqlite deployment.sqlite --profile <your profile> data-finops serve --db deployment.sqlite The copy is a snapshot. To get the data of a later run, download it again. The download requires s3:GetObject on the database object, which neither output policy gives. If kmsKeyArn is set, it also requires kms:Decrypt on the key. serve shows the full Billing Line unless you pass --explanation-detail minimal. Switch the API off If you set both rate limits of the API to 0, API Gateway answers 429 to each request, and the API function does not run. The data does not change. Record the limits in the stack, then run pulumi up: pulumi config set apiRateLimit 0 pulumi config set apiBurstLimit 0 pulumi up --policy-pack policy To switch the API back on, remove the two settings with pulumi config rm and run pulumi up again. A reserved concurrency of 0 (apiReservedConcurrency) also stops the API function, but API Gateway then answers each request with an error.

title: Tear down a Deployment
text: pulumi destroy removes a Deployment. By default it keeps the bucket, with the database and the Inbox in it, so a mistaken destroy loses no data. This guide removes a Deployment either way and lists what is left behind. Owner-run: not run on this page. Every command here reaches a real AWS account, and the deploy creates resources that cost money. Only the account owner runs pulumi preview, pulumi up and pulumi destroy against a real account. The owner can follow this page by hand, or run it as one wizard: teardown.sh. The wizard does these things: It runs each step below. It also tears down the reference workload. It checks that the state of each stack is empty. It checks that the main resources are gone in AWS. These are the functions, the producer, reader, consumer and operator policies, and the bucket if you chose to delete it. They also include the bucket, Glue database, workgroup and Budget of the reference workload. It asks before each step that changes something. It masks account IDs, buckets, profiles and the URL of the API in all that it shows and records. From the root of the repository, run the wizard: bash infra/pulumi/aws/wizards/teardown.sh On Windows, it requires Git Bash, not the bash of WSL. Its masked record is written to .local/. Before you destroy Detach the producer, reader, consumer and operator policies from every identity they were attached to. IAM refuses to delete a managed policy that is still attached, and the destroy stops there: aws iam list-entities-for-policy --policy-arn <producerPolicyArn> --profile <admin profile> aws iam list-entities-for-policy --policy-arn <readerPolicyArn> --profile <admin profile> aws iam list-entities-for-policy --policy-arn <consumerPolicyArn> --profile <admin profile> aws iam list-entities-for-policy --policy-arn <operatorPolicyArn> --profile <admin profile> aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name <role> --policy-arn <policy arn> --profile <admin profile> Run every command below from infra/pulumi/aws, with PULUMI_BACKEND_URL and PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE set as in Deploy to AWS. Destroy and keep the data pulumi destroy This command deletes the functions, their log groups and roles, the schedule and the API Gateway API. It also deletes the producer, reader, consumer and operator policies, the alarm and its topic, the Budget, and the Lambda package object. S3 Versioning keeps the last version of the package, about 66 MB, until it expires after noncurrentVersionDays. The command keeps the bucket and each setting on it: the public access blocks, encryption, versioning, the expiry rules and the TLS-only policy. The bucket leaves the state of the stack. Thus a later pulumi up tries to create a new bucket with a new name, and does not adopt this bucket. While the bucket is kept, AWS bills its storage, and its expiry rules continue to operate. Inbox objects expire after inboxRetentionDays, and old object versions expire after noncurrentVersionDays. To delete the bucket later, empty it in the S3 console, which deletes each version. Then delete the bucket. Destroy and delete the data To delete the bucket with everything in it, every version included, change the setting and apply it first. The stack records whether to keep the bucket when it is deployed, not when it is destroyed: pulumi config set deleteDataOnDestroy true pulumi up pulumi destroy This cannot be undone. If you think that you will want the database later, download it first. See Read a Deployment. What is left The stack's local state, in .local/pulumi. Remove the empty stack with pulumi stack rm dev. The package, infra/pulumi/aws/build/data-finops-lambda.zip, which is git-ignored. The deployer identity and its profile, which the owner created and removes. Anything a producer or reader set up on its own side, such as an OpenLineage configuration that writes to the Inbox. The FOCUS export and the Athena workgroups, which the Deployment only read. The reference workload is a separate stack with its own teardown: see Deploy the reference workload.

title: Reference
text: Reference describes what data-finops offers, exactly and completely.

title: Command line
text: Every data-finops command, with its usage and its arguments. This page is generated from the command line's own parser, so it says what data-finops --help says. Run data-finops <command> --help for the same text in a terminal. --db names the database file that each command reads and writes. The first use creates the file. serve requires the optional api extra. title: HTTP API
text: Every route that data-finops serve answers, with its parameters and responses. This page is generated from schemas/openapi.json, the OpenAPI 3.1 document the server is tested against. Amounts are Decimal strings, never floating-point numbers. Errors are Problem Details (RFC 9457, application/problem+json). They name the field at fault and never echo what was sent. The server listens on loopback unless told otherwise. If a token is configured, each route requires Authorization: Bearer <token>. Lists are paged with limit (default 100, at most 1000) and offset. GET /health: Health Whether the database opens as a current data-finops database. Status Meaning Body 200 Successful Response application/json: Health 401 When a token is configured: no valid bearer token (ADR 0024). application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) 503 The database cannot be opened. application/json: Health GET /v1/costs/summary: Cost Summary One Cost Summary per Snapshot Scope, for the scope's current Allocation Snapshot. With calculation_run_id, the response has only the summary of that run's snapshot, which can be current or superseded. Parameter In Required Type Meaning cost_basis query optional CostBasis: one of "BilledCost", "EffectiveCost", "ListCost", "ContractedCost", default "BilledCost" calculation_run_id query optional string, at most 128 characters, or null billing_account_id query optional string, at most 128 characters, or null billing_period query optional string, date, or null source query optional string, at most 256 characters, or null Status Meaning Body 200 Successful Response application/json: CostSummaries 400 Invalid request, or a Calculation Run named together with scope filters: the detail names the fields, never their values. application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) 401 When a token is configured: no valid bearer token (ADR 0024). application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) 500 An unexpected failure. The detail tells nothing about it. application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) 503 The database cannot be opened as a current data-finops database. application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) 404 No such Calculation Run. A filter that matches no scope gives an empty list. application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) GET /v1/allocations: Allocations One page of one Allocation Snapshot. It is the snapshot of a named Calculation Run. If no run is named, it is the current snapshot of the single Snapshot Scope that billing_account_id, billing_period and source select. Parameter In Required Type Meaning calculation_run_id query optional string, at most 128 characters, or null billing_account_id query optional string, at most 128 characters, or null billing_period query optional string, date, or null source query optional string, at most 256 characters, or null target_id query optional string, at most 256 characters, or null category query optional AllocationCategory: one of "direct", "shared", "idle", "unallocated", or null billing_line_ref query optional string, at most 256 characters, or null cost_basis query optional CostBasis: one of "BilledCost", "EffectiveCost", "ListCost", "ContractedCost", or null limit query optional integer, 1 to 1000, default 100 offset query optional integer, at least 0, default 0 Status Meaning Body 200 Successful Response application/json: AllocationPage 400 Invalid request, or filters that match more than one Snapshot Scope: the detail names the fields to give, never their values. application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) 401 When a token is configured: no valid bearer token (ADR 0024). application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) 500 An unexpected failure. The detail tells nothing about it. application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) 503 The database cannot be opened as a current data-finops database. application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) 404 No such Calculation Run, or no calculated Snapshot Scope matches. application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) GET /v1/rollups: Rollups What each Model Execution or Workload Run cost in one Allocation Snapshot, selected as for /v1/allocations. This route is separate, because a Roll-up is a view, never an Allocation. This is the default endpoint of the OpenLineage HTTP transport (spec 04). The event is screened exactly as one item of an event file. This is the one async endpoint (spec 06). Send the event uncompressed. application/problem+json: Problem Details (RFC 9457) 500 An unexpected failure.
