title: Exit codes and environment
text: This page lists the exit codes of the data-finops command and the environment variables data-finops reads. A test checks both lists against the code. Exit codes Every data-finops command exits with one of these codes. 0 Everything was stored. OpenLineage events of a kind data-finops does not read are listed as unsupported, and they do not change the code. For serve and demo, 0 means the server stopped normally. 1 A workload input was rejected, in whole or in part. Only ingest openlineage, ingest dbt, ingest athena and collect exit with 1. If some items were rejected, the rest were stored. Each rejected item is named by its position and the reason. If the whole file was rejected, nothing was stored, and the message gives the reason. Messages never quote the input's content. 2 Nothing was done, and the message says why. These are the causes: The arguments were wrong. A file could not be read or written. calculate or serve was given a --db path with no database file there. The database file is not a data-finops database. A FOCUS file is not a FOCUS Export Snapshot or a usable AWS Data Exports Delivery. serve refused to start, for example because of the token rules below. collect was given a settings file it refuses. collect could not read a source, for example because AWS denied access. This is the one 2 after which something was done: collect still collected the other sources and calculated Allocations. --help exits with 0. Environment variables DATA_FINOPS_TOKEN The bearer token for serve. When a token is set, each route requires the header Authorization: Bearer <token>, also the API documentation. Without one, every route is open. Set the token in this variable or in a file named by --token-file, not both. If both are set, serve exits with 2. The spaces and line breaks at the start and end of the token are removed. What remains must be at least 16 characters. A shorter token makes serve exit with 2. serve requires a token to listen on an address other than loopback, such as --host 0.0.0.0. A name such as localhost does not count as loopback. demo ignores the token. It always serves on loopback, with every route open. data-finops never logs, prints or stores the token. Errors say what is wrong with it, not what it is. DATA_FINOPS_COLLECTOR_SETTINGS A Deployment's collector function reads its settings from this variable: JSON with the keys of the collect settings file, validated the same way. The stack sets it. An unset, unreadable or invalid value fails the invocation, and the error names the setting at fault, never its value. DATA_FINOPS_BUCKET The Deployment's bucket, for its API function and the public demo's simulator and publisher. The API function serves a copy of the database object in it, and the publisher publishes a copy. The simulator writes its records to the Inbox in it. The stack sets it. DATA_FINOPS_EXPLANATION_DETAIL How much of the Billing Line a Deployment's API shows in a Cost Explanation: minimal (the default) or full (ADR 0028). The stack sets it from its explanationDetail setting. DATA_FINOPS_DEMO_BUCKET The public demo's bucket, for the dataset generator and the publisher. The generator writes the demo dataset in it, under dataset/. The publisher writes the Demo Snapshot in it. The stack sets it when publicDemo is true. If it is not set, the invocation fails, and the error names the variable. DATA_FINOPS_ANON_SECRET The secret for the two anonymizer scripts. They are for contributors and are not part of the data-finops command. scripts/anonymize_focus_export.py anonymizes a downloaded AWS FOCUS export. scripts/anonymize_workload_outputs.py anonymizes the reference workload's Athena history, dbt artifacts and OpenLineage events. The rules for the secret: The secret keys the pseudonyms. The same secret always gives the same pseudonym for the same value. Use one secret for both scripts, so that billing and workload data still match after the anonymization. It must not be empty. If it is empty or unset, the script stops before it writes anything. Keep it, and never commit it.

title: Deployment settings
text: The settings of the AWS Deployment and the outputs of its Pulumi stack. Each setting is a key of the stack's configuration: aws:region, and every other key under data-finops:. A setting left out takes its default. The stack checks every setting before it declares anything, and an error names the setting, never its value. This page is generated from the stack's source, deployment/settings.py and deployment/program.py, which are authoritative. Settings Key Default Meaning aws:region required The AWS Region to deploy to. The collector reads the Athena workgroups in this Region. exportBucket required The S3 bucket the AWS Data Exports FOCUS export is delivered to. The collector only reads it. exportName required The name of the FOCUS export, as AWS Data Exports names it. workgroups required The Athena workgroups whose query history is collected, as a JSON list of names, for example ["primary"]. It must not be empty. exportPrefix empty The S3 path prefix that the export is delivered under. It is empty when the export has no prefix. billingLookbackPeriods 2 How many Billing Periods each Collection Run lists, back from the current one. A whole number from 1 to 24. maxHistoryPages 200 How many ListQueryExecutions pages each Collection Run reads, per workgroup. A whole number from 1 to 1000. schedule cron(0 6 * * ? *) When the Collection Run starts, as an EventBridge Scheduler expression, in UTC. collectorTimeoutSeconds 900 The collector function's timeout, in seconds. A whole number from 1 to 900. collectorMemoryMb 2048 The collector function's memory, in MB. A whole number from 128 to 10240. apiTimeoutSeconds 30 The API function's timeout, in seconds. API Gateway stops a request after 30 seconds, so a longer timeout does not give a request more time. A whole number from 1 to 900. apiMemoryMb 1024 The API function's memory, in MB. A whole number from 128 to 10240. ephemeralStorageMb 10240 The /tmp storage, in MB, of each function that copies the database: the collector, the API and the publisher. The database and each Inbox file must fit in it. Lambda charges for the storage above 512 MB. A whole number from 512 to 10240. apiReservedConcurrency unset An optional limit on the concurrent requests of the API function, a whole number of at least 0. 0 switches the API off. New accounts can lack the concurrency quota to reserve any. apiRateLimit 10 The most requests a second that the API accepts, from all callers together. API Gateway answers 429 to more. Set it and apiBurstLimit to 0 to switch the API off (the kill switch). A whole number from 0 to 10000. apiBurstLimit 20 The most requests that the API accepts in one short burst, from all callers together. A whole number from 0 to 5000. logRetentionDays 30 How long both functions' logs are kept, in days: a period CloudWatch Logs accepts, such as 1, 7, 14, 30, 90 or 365. noncurrentVersionDays 30 How long an old version of the database object is kept, in days, before S3 expires it. A whole number from 1 to 3650. inboxRetentionDays 30 How long an object stays in the Inbox, in days, before S3 expires it. A whole number from 1 to 3650. kmsKeyArn unset An optional customer-managed KMS key ARN to encrypt the bucket with, at about $1 a month. Use the key ARN, arn:aws:kms:<region>:<account>:key/<key id>. An alias ARN is refused, because IAM gives the use of a key only on its key ARN. Unset, the bucket uses the S3-managed key. explanationDetail minimal How much the API's Cost Explanations show: minimal or full (ADR 0028). budgetMonthlyUsd unset An optional monthly amount, in US dollars, for an account-wide AWS Budget that alerts on forecast and actual spend. AWS Budgets cover the whole account, not just the Deployment. Give it with budgetEmail, or neither. budgetEmail unset The address the Budget alerts are sent to. Give it with budgetMonthlyUsd, or neither. alarmEmail unset An optional address to send an alarm to when the collector function reports errors, through an SNS topic. deleteDataOnDestroy false Whether pulumi destroy deletes the bucket and its data. By default the bucket is kept, with the database and the Inbox in it. costDimensions unset An optional path to a Cost Dimensions file (TOML, spec 09). The stack uploads it to config/cost-dimensions.toml in the bucket, and the collector applies it in each Collection Run. Unset, no dimensions apply. publicDemo false Whether the stack also makes the public demo (spec 09). The demo has its own bucket, the data-finops-demo Athena workgroup, the Glue tables of the demo dataset and the dataset generator function. Set it to false and run pulumi up to remove the demo. demoScanCutoffBytes 1000000000 The most bytes one query in the demo workgroup can scan before Athena cancels it. Athena accepts 10 MB or more. A whole number from 10000000 to 1000000000000. demoSchedule cron(25 0/6 * * ? *) When the demo's simulated orchestrator starts, in UTC: every six hours, as cron(M H/6 * * ? *). M, from 10 to 40, keeps each query away from the hour (spec 09). H, from 0 to 5, is the first start of the day, which runs daily_orders, and weekly_finance on Mondays. Each start runs hourly_events. Outputs Output Meaning bucket The Deployment's S3 bucket: the database, the Inboxes and the Lambda package. apiUrl The API's address, on API Gateway. Requests must be signed with AWS SigV4 (service execute-api) by a principal with the reader, consumer or operator policy. producerPolicyArn The managed policy that lets a producer write to the Inboxes and nothing else. Attach it to whatever sends OpenLineage events or dbt artifacts. readerPolicyArn The managed policy that lets a principal call the API's read routes. consumerPolicyArn The managed policy of the consumer Control Role. For now, it lets a principal call the read routes only. operatorPolicyArn The managed policy of the operator Control Role. For now, it lets a principal call the read routes only. collectorFunction The collector function's name, for its logs or to invoke a Collection Run by hand. apiFunction The API function's name, for its logs. demoUrl Only with publicDemo: the public demo's address, on CloudFront. demoBucket Only with publicDemo: the public demo's bucket, with the demo dataset. demoGeneratorFunction Only with publicDemo: the function that writes the demo dataset. Invoke it one time after the first deploy. demoSimulatorFunction Only with publicDemo: the simulated orchestrator, which its schedule starts. Invoke it by hand to run the DAGs due now.

title: Glossary
text: The terms data-finops uses, in its pages, its API and its code. Most terms also give the words to avoid. This page is generated from GLOSSARY.md. Attributes authoritative cloud charges to the data workloads that caused them. It never creates money, loses money or counts money more than one time. The terms here are settled. Contested terms are in docs/implementation/open-questions.md until they are resolved. Billing Billing Line One FOCUS row from a provider's billing export: an authoritative charge in one billing currency for one charge period, with each FOCUS cost column. It is the unit that Reconciliation partitions exactly once. Avoid: bill row, invoice line, cost record Export Snapshot The complete set of Billing Lines a provider published for one billing account, Billing Period and source at one point in time. A restatement replaces the whole snapshot. Earlier snapshots are kept. Avoid: file, batch, version (alone) Delivery One AWS Data Exports execution: the data files and manifests AWS writes for one billing period at one time. Read as one Export Snapshot, published when AWS created the execution (ADR 0020). Avoid: export (for one execution), drop, upload Superseded Snapshot An Export Snapshot kept as history because a later publication is current for its Snapshot Scope. Avoid: old version, stale snapshot Snapshot Scope The billing account, Billing Period and source an Export Snapshot covers, and so the Allocation Snapshots computed from it. At most one Export Snapshot and one Allocation Snapshot are current for a Snapshot Scope. Avoid: partition, key (alone) Billing Period The invoice period of the provider that a Billing Line belongs to. It can be different from the charge period of the line. Avoid: month (alone) Cost Basis Which FOCUS cost column a figure is taken from (for example BilledCost or EffectiveCost). Amounts in different cost bases are never added together. Avoid: cost type, price Adjustment A Billing Line that corrects or reduces charges: a credit, refund or discount (FOCUS ChargeCategory Credit or Adjustment). Adjustments are their own lines, signed, and can be negative. Tax and purchase lines are not Adjustments. Avoid: rebate (unless the provider uses that term), negative cost Cost Pool A set of eligible Billing Lines with one currency, cost basis, time window and pricing category, whose workloads give the weights. Each Billing Line in the pool is partitioned by those weights. The pool itself is not the partitioned amount. Avoid: bucket, cost group Eligibility Whether an allocator that exists can allocate a Billing Line to workloads. Ineligible lines remain Unallocated. Workload identity Query Execution One provider-recorded execution of a query, identified by the provider's query execution ID within an account and region. Avoid: query (alone), job Model Execution One run of a dbt node within one dbt invocation. A dbt node ID alone never identifies an execution. Avoid: model run, dbt job dbt Node A model, seed, test or other resource declared in a dbt project's manifest, identified by its node ID within one invocation's manifest. A dbt Node is a declaration. Its execution in an invocation is a Model Execution. Avoid: model (alone), dbt object Workload Run One orchestrated execution that an orchestrator or lineage Producer reports, for example an Airflow task run. It can have a parent run (the run that directly contains it) and a root run (the top of its chain, for example the DAG run). Avoid: job, task (alone), pipeline run Identity Link An assertion that two workload identities (for example a Query Execution and a Model Execution) are the same unit of work, together with the Evidence for it. Avoid: match, correlation (alone), join Evidence The explicit identifier or trusted metadata that justifies an Identity Link or an Allocation. Time overlap alone is never Evidence. Avoid: signal, heuristic Trusted Query Comment The dbt comment at the very start of a query's text that names the dbt Node and invocation that issued it. A comment anywhere else in the text is not Evidence. Avoid: query tag, query header Link Outcome What became of an attempt to link a workload identity: linked (exactly one counterpart), override (a person recorded the link with an Override), no evidence, unmatched (Evidence names a counterpart nobody reported) or ambiguous (more than one candidate). Only linked and override make an Identity Link. Avoid: match status, correlation result Lineage Data Asset A dataset or other data object that workloads read or write, identified within a namespace. Avoid: table (alone), entity Lineage Edge An observed read or write relationship between a Workload Run and a Data Asset. Lineage has no financial authority. Avoid: dependency (alone) Allocation Allocation The portion of one Billing Line, in one Cost Basis, assigned to one Allocation Target, with its method, Evidence and policy version. A Cost Pool only supplies the weights. Avoid: charge, cost (alone) Allocation Target What an Allocation is assigned to: a Query Execution, or one of the synthetic targets Idle or Unallocated. Model Executions and Workload Runs receive cost only as Roll-ups. Avoid: owner, cost center, tenant, data product, consumer (not targets in the MVP) Cost Dimension A business attribute an organization configures to group its cost by, such as team or tenant. Its value is a claim with a recorded source, never Evidence. A dimension is a view: it does not change how a Billing Line is partitioned (ADR 0031). Avoid: attribution plane, tag (alone), label, Allocation Target Roll-up The sum of Allocations over the Query Executions linked to a Model Execution, a Workload Run or a higher group. A Roll-up is a view, never a further Allocation. Avoid: re-allocation, inherited cost Cost Summary Where one Allocation Snapshot put the bill, for each currency and for one Cost Basis. It gives the billed total, the allocated amounts by Allocation Category and Confidence, the Unallocated amounts by reason, the Adjustments, and the Reconciliation Delta. Avoid: overview, total cost, spend report Cost Explanation The chain behind one Allocation. It gives the Billing Line, and the method, Confidence and Coverage of the Allocation. It also gives its Evidence resolved to Query Execution, Model Execution and Workload Runs, and the Roll-ups that it contributes to. Avoid: drilldown, trace, breakdown, query cost Billing Line Detail How much of a Billing Line a Cost Explanation shows: minimal or full (ADR 0028). minimal withholds tags and free-text names, and it is the default of a Deployment and of the Public Demo. Avoid: redaction level, verbosity Allocation Category The kind of share an Allocation represents: direct (from the target's own metered usage), shared, idle or unallocated. Avoid: kind, type Metered Share A direct Allocation of an aggregated Billing Line, apportioned by each Query Execution's billable usage. It is an estimate, never an exact price. Avoid: query cost, exact cost Billable Usage The quantity a provider charges a Query Execution for, after the provider's minimums and rounding. It can differ from the quantity the query actually used. Avoid: scanned bytes (unless that is what is billed) Billing Scope The Query Executions whose usage a Billing Line can bill: those of its account, region and charge period (ADR 0023). If the line bills by workgroup, its Billing Scope has only that workgroup's Query Executions. It is an accounting scope, not Evidence. Avoid: matching window, time overlap Coverage The fraction of a Billing Line's billed usage quantity accounted for by the Billable Usage of known Query Executions in the line's Billing Scope, linked or not. Only the covered fraction can become Metered Shares. Avoid: match rate, completeness percentage Query-history Completeness Coverage of exactly one for a Billing Line: every billable Query Execution in its Billing Scope is known. Avoid: full history Confidence A categorical grade of Evidence quality for an allocated amount: direct_verified, metered_estimate or heuristic_estimate. It does not apply to Unallocated amounts and is never a probability. Avoid: score, likelihood Idle A synthetic Allocation Target for cost of capacity that was paid for but had no observed activity. Avoid: waste, unused (alone) Unallocated A synthetic Allocation Target for cost whose Evidence is not there, is ambiguous or is ineligible. It is shown, never hidden or guessed. Avoid: unknown, other, misc Allocation Policy A versioned, documented set of rules that decides Eligibility, weights and how remainders are handled. Every Allocation records the policy version that produced it. Avoid: rules engine, config Calculation Run One deterministic execution of the Allocation Policy over a fixed set of inputs. Avoid: job, batch Input Digest The value that identifies what one Calculation Run read. It covers the Export Snapshot's lines and pools, the Billable Usage and Evidence of the Query Executions in scope, and each policy version. The Cost Dimensions configuration is not part of it (Q72). Avoid: hash (alone), checksum Reconciliation Reconciliation The check that what the product holds equals its authoritative source exactly, for each Billing Line, currency and Cost Basis. It checks the Ledger against the imported Export Snapshot, and Allocations against the Billing Lines that they partition. Avoid: balancing, matching Reconciliation Delta The signed difference between the authoritative amount and what is held against it (the Ledger's amount, or the sum of Allocations), in one currency. It is zero when Reconciliation holds. Ledger The immutable, versioned record of Export Snapshots and the Allocation Snapshots computed from them. One of each is current, and all are kept. Avoid: the Database (the Ledger is one part of it), warehouse Allocation Snapshot The complete set of Allocations produced by one Calculation Run. Any period can be calculated again. A new calculation with different inputs creates a new snapshot and moves the current pointer. A Replay of the current snapshot stores nothing. Avoid: result, rerun output Replay An import of an Export Snapshot whose content equals the current snapshot of its Snapshot Scope, or equals a snapshot stored under the same ID (ADR 0020). A Calculation Run whose Input Digest equals the current Allocation Snapshot's is also a Replay, and neither stores anything. Avoid: duplicate (that is one item), rerun Stores Database The one SQLite file that holds what data-finops stores, such as the Ledger and the Workload Store, locally or in a Deployment. In a Deployment, it is one object in the Deployment's bucket. Avoid: store (alone), warehouse Workload Store The record of workload metadata as Producers and providers reported it: OpenLineage events, dbt artifacts and Query Executions, each kept as an Observation. It is in the Database beside the Ledger. Avoid: telemetry database, metadata warehouse Observation One stored report of a Workload Run, a Model Execution or a Query Execution, as one Producer or provider sent it. Observations are kept as they arrived, and are never merged. Avoid: row, event (for a stored report) Duplicate An item that arrives again with the same content as an Observation that is already stored. Nothing new is stored. Avoid: replay (that is a whole snapshot) Changed Copy An item that arrives again with different content, for example the same event or Query Execution reported in a new form. It is kept beside the first Observation, and the item is flagged for Observations that conflict. Avoid: update (for an item), overwrite Deployment Deployment One Pulumi stack of data-finops in one AWS account (ADR 0026, spec 08). Avoid: install, environment Collection Run One execution of the collector: it fetches every source a Deployment reads, ingests it, then starts a Calculation Run for each Snapshot Scope. Avoid: job, sync, refresh Inbox The bucket prefix Producers write OpenLineage events and dbt artifacts to, for the next Collection Run to pull (ADR 0027). Avoid: drop zone, landing area Producer A system that sends workload metadata to data-finops: an OpenLineage emitter such as Airflow, or the dbt process whose artifacts are sent. In a Deployment, a Producer writes only to the Inbox. Avoid: client, agent, source (for the system that sends) Collection Watermark What a Deployment has already collected, for each source: the Delivery folders ingested, the Athena query IDs stored, and the Inbox objects processed. Inbox objects are keyed by key and ETag, so an overwritten object is collected again. It is never a clock time alone. Avoid: checkpoint, cursor Public Demo The hosted, read-only dashboard over the demo workgroup's share of a Deployment's bill, served as a static snapshot to anyone (ADR 0029, spec 09). Avoid: hosted dashboard, live site Demo Snapshot One published set of the read model's answers for the Public Demo, written after a Collection Run and swapped in whole. Avoid: cache, export Simulated Orchestrator The scheduled function that plays Airflow and dbt for the Public Demo. It runs believable DAGs whose models issue real Athena queries with real Trusted Query Comments. It writes their OpenLineage events and dbt artifacts to the Inbox (ADR 0030). Avoid: fake Airflow, mock workload Control plane Control Plane The CLI commands, API routes and Deployment Dashboard actions that configure, run, inspect and correct a local Database or a Deployment (ADR 0032). Avoid: admin panel, management API Command One recorded request to change what data-finops holds or does, such as a run, a new Cost Dimensions version or an Override. The collector applies it, or rejects it with a reason. It is never changed after it is written. Avoid: job, request (alone), action (alone) Override A recorded replacement of one input of a Calculation Run, a Cost Dimension value or an Identity Link, for one open Billing Period or from a period onward. It never changes a billed amount. Avoid: adjustment (that is a Billing Line), manual allocation, correction (alone) Control Role What a person or principal can do in the Control Plane: reader, consumer or operator. Avoid: permission level, user type Deployment Dashboard The dashboard of one Deployment, served behind a sign-in, with the actions of the viewer's Control Role. It is not the Public Demo. Avoid: hosted dashboard, admin console Flagged ambiguities "Query cost" implies an exact per-query price that providers do not bill. Say "Allocation to a Query Execution" and state its Confidence. "Consumer" is a Control Role. The Allocation Target _Avoid_ line uses "consumer" for a data consumer as a target, which is a different thing. "Owner" is not a term (Q156). override dimension --owner names the Cost Dimension that the configuration marks as the owner. "Unknown" is used in fixtures as a target name. The domain term is Unallocated. no_evidence names two things: a Link Outcome (a Query Execution without a Trusted Query Comment) and an Unallocated reason (a shared pool with no positive weight, #86). They never meet: Link Outcomes describe Identity Links, Unallocated reasons describe money. Say which one you mean. **Lineage Edge** was defined as a Workload Run's read or write of a Data Asset "or between two Data Assets". Only run-to-asset edges are stored (contracts.workload.LineageEdge), so the definition was narrowed to them (#207). Column-level lineage is the eventual goal (owner, 2026-11-07). It will require its own design and terms.

title: Explanation
text: Explanation covers why data-finops works the way it does. Each page cites the decision records and specifications behind it, which stay authoritative.

title: The bill is authoritative
headings: Metadata moves money, never makes it
What cannot be explained stays Unallocated
Each Cost Basis reconciles on its own
text: data-finops never decides how much something cost. The cloud provider's bill does. Workload metadata only decides where the bill's money goes. This page explains that rule and how data-finops checks it. The decisions are in ADR 0003, ADR 0015 and ADR 0016, and the pipeline is in spec 03. They stay authoritative. Metadata moves money, never makes it A provider's bill arrives as an Export Snapshot of Billing Lines, kept in the Ledger exactly as published: every cost column, credits, currencies and revisions. A Calculation Run splits each Billing Line into Allocations. Query history, dbt artifacts and OpenLineage events say which Query Execution used what. They never add a cent. A Query Execution that scanned more takes a larger share of its Billing Line, but the amount to share is always what the provider billed. So an Allocation can be an estimate, while the totals stay exact. Every Billing Line is split exactly once, and its Allocations sum to its amount, negative Adjustments included. What cannot be explained stays Unallocated Money with no Evidence is not spread over whatever ran nearby. It becomes Unallocated, with its reason, and is shown, never hidden or guessed. In the tutorial's bill, the $4.00 S3 storage line stays Unallocated as ineligible, because no Allocation Policy allocates storage yet. A bill that is half Unallocated is still a true bill. A bill whose Unallocated money has been quietly spread is not. Above a Query Execution, nothing is allocated again. A Model Execution or a Workload Run gets money only as a Roll-up: a sum of the Allocations linked to it. So a Roll-up can never hold more than the bill gave out. Reconciliation proves it Reconciliation is exact, for each Billing Line, currency and Cost Basis. It is checked in two places: For a loaded Export Snapshot, each stored Billing Line equals the provider's line, in each Cost Basis. Each load checks this: data-finops ingest focus and each Collection Run. If a line differs, the load is rejected, and the Ledger keeps nothing of the snapshot. Rows are never deduplicated, so nothing the provider billed is lost (ADR 0019). After a Calculation Run, the Allocations must sum to the Billing Lines. The Reconciliation Delta is the signed difference, and it is zero when Reconciliation holds. /v1/reconciliation reports it. An Allocation to a Billing Line that is not in the bill, or in the wrong currency, counts against a billed amount of zero. Thus invented money shows as a delta and cannot hide. Each Cost Basis reconciles on its own A FOCUS Billing Line has more than one cost column, for example BilledCost and EffectiveCost. Each one is reconciled separately, and none is derived from another. The default view is BilledCost, because it matches the invoice. EffectiveCost, which spreads commitments and discounts, can be selected instead. See HTTP API for the cost_basis parameter.

title: Allocation and Coverage
headings: The same inputs give the same Allocations
A Metered Share requires measured Coverage
Billing scope is accounting, not Evidence
text: This page explains how a Calculation Run splits a Billing Line, and why it splits a metered line only as far as Coverage allows. The decisions are in ADR 0007, ADR 0016, ADR 0017 and ADR 0023, and the rules are in spec 03. They stay authoritative. The same inputs give the same Allocations A Calculation Run is deterministic. It uses decimal amounts, stable rounding and a versioned Allocation Policy. If you run it again on the same inputs, it stores nothing new. A changed policy gets a new version. The Allocations that the policy made before keep the old version. Thus you can trace each number to the rules that made it. Three Allocation Targets Every Allocation goes to one of three Allocation Targets: a Query Execution: the unit that a provider actually bills for Idle: capacity that was paid for but had no observed activity Unallocated: money with no Evidence, named with its reason A Model Execution or Workload Run is never a target. It gets money only as a Roll-up over its Identity Links. Failed and retried work is charged to its Query Execution and shown with its status, so a failure's cost stays visible. A Metered Share requires measured Coverage An Athena on-demand Billing Line bills a quantity of data scanned. Each Query Execution in the line's billing scope has a Billable Usage: what the provider bills for it, which is not always what it scanned. Coverage compares the two: Coverage = known Billable Usage ÷ the Billing Line's billed quantity. At Coverage 1, the line is split by Billable Usage. Each share is a Metered Share: Allocation Category direct, Confidence metered_estimate. Below 1, the history is not complete. Only the covered fraction is split. The remainder is Unallocated as coverage_remainder. It is not spread over the Query Executions that are known. Above 1, the known history claims more than was billed, which means something is wrong. The whole line is Unallocated as coverage_exceeded, and flagged. Coverage counts as 1 within half a unit of the last digit the provider bills in. A Metered Share is an estimate, so it is never labeled as exact. Billing scope is accounting, not Evidence A Query Execution is in the billing scope of a Billing Line when these conditions are true: It ran in the usage account and Region of the line. It ran in the workgroup of the line, if the line names a workgroup. It completed in the charge period of the line. Then the Query Execution gets a share of the cost of the line. The billing scope does not show which Model Execution ran it. A Query Execution with no Identity Link still counts toward Coverage and still gets its Metered Share. It only has no Roll-up (ADR 0023). A worked example The tutorial's bill has one Athena Billing Line of $6.00, for 0.001 TB scanned in workgroup demo. Two Query Executions are in its billing scope: q-001 succeeded and scanned 1,000,000,000 bytes. Its Billable Usage is 0.000905 TB: 10 9 / 2 40 is 0.00090949 TB, and its hour is rounded down to a multiple of 0.000005 TB. q-002 is DDL that scanned 0 bytes. Its Billable Usage is 0. Known Billable Usage is 0.000905 TB. The bill exports 0.001 TB with three decimal places, so a difference of 0.0005 TB or less counts as the same quantity. Thus Coverage is 1. q-001 gets a $6.00 Metered Share. Its Trusted Query Comment names Model Execution model.demo.orders, so the $6.00 rolls up to it. The bill's $4.00 S3 storage line is outside every policy, so it is Unallocated as ineligible. The current Athena policy Calculation Runs record their policy version, today allocation-engine/1+line-classification/1+athena-billable-usage/3+athena-billing-scope/2+cost-dimensions/1. athena-billable-usage/3 sets each Query Execution's Billable Usage: a failed one, or one that scanned 0 bytes: 0 any other one that succeeded or was canceled: the bytes that it scanned / 2 40 TB, with a minimum of 0.00001 TB. The queries that completed in the same UTC hour are added, and that sum is rounded down to a multiple of 0.000005 TB. Each query gets a part of the hour's sum, in proportion to its quantity after the minimum. a queued one, or one that is still in progress: 0 in that report a billed one that reported no scan: unknown AWS does not state the units of the bill's TB. Version 3 reads 1 TB as 2 40 bytes, because only that fits the owner's real lines (issue #310). Version 2 read 1 TB as 10 12 bytes, and rounded each query up to the next MB, with a minimum of 10 MB. These rules were checked against a real FOCUS export in issue #91. It showed that a query that scans nothing bills nothing, whatever its statement type, so version 2 replaced version 1, which charged such queries 10 MB. Allocations made under version 1 keep it. A Billing Line can cover more than one hour, and its billing scope is its whole charge period. Athena billed two queries that finished seconds before an hour ended in the next hour's line. A query that finishes that close to an hour boundary can be scoped to the wrong line, which then stays Unallocated rather than misallocated (open question 25).

title: Identity Links and Evidence
headings: The cost of no Identity Link
text: A Roll-up says which Model Execution or Workload Run an Allocation adds up to. It is only as good as the link behind it. This page explains what counts as Evidence for an Identity Link, and what happens when there is none. The decisions are in ADR 0006 and ADR 0022, with details in spec 03 and spec 04. They stay authoritative. Only explicit Evidence links An Identity Link connects the records of one piece of work in different systems. These records are a Query Execution in the history of Athena, the Model Execution in dbt's run results, and the Workload Runs in OpenLineage events. It requires explicit Evidence: an exact provider ID, or metadata from a trusted source. Time overlap is never Evidence. A Query Execution that overlaps a dbt run can belong to any work. The Trusted Query Comment dbt artifacts do not name the Athena Query Executions a Model Execution issued. The Evidence comes from Athena's side instead. dbt can send a query comment before each statement, and data-finops trusts it only at the very start of the query text. That Trusted Query Comment names the dbt invocation and node. Only those two values are kept. The rest of the query text is dropped. dbt's default comment has no invocation_id, so it must be configured. The configuration is in the reference workload's README. dbt-athena sends statements that start with alter, drop, optimize, vacuum or msck without the comment, so those have no Identity Link. An OpenLineage run from dbt-ol links to its Model Execution by the dbt node and invocation it reports. Workload Runs link to their parents and roots as the events name them. Link Outcomes Each claim a Query Execution makes has a Link Outcome: linked: the claim names a known Model Execution. This is an Identity Link. no_evidence: there is no Trusted Query Comment. unmatched: the comment names a dbt node and invocation that no run results report. ambiguous: there is more than one candidate, for example, reports of one Query Execution that name different Model Executions. No Identity Link is made. Links are worked out when they are asked for, from what is stored, so the order the inputs arrive in never changes them. In the tutorial, q-004's reports disagree, so its Link Outcome is ambiguous, and model.demo.customers, which only q-004 claims, gets no Roll-up. The Link Outcome no_evidence is not the Unallocated reason no_evidence. Always say which one you mean. Stored as reported, never merged OpenLineage runs are stored exactly as each event reported them. They are linked, never merged into one record. A report that is different from an earlier report is kept next to it, as a separate observation. Thus no report silently replaces another. Two reports of one Query Execution that name different Model Executions also get a flag. A Model Execution comes only from dbt's run results, never from an OpenLineage event alone. The cost of no Identity Link If there is no Identity Link, the money still goes to the same place. A Query Execution without one still gets its share of the Billing Line, because billing scope is accounting, not Evidence (ADR 0023). It only has no Roll-up to a Model Execution or Workload Run. Thus a broken comment configuration shows as Allocations that roll up to nothing. It does not show as Allocations given to the wrong Model Execution.

title: Export Snapshots and restatements
headings: The whole Export Snapshot is the unit
Allocations follow, and keep their history
text: Providers publish a Billing Period's bill more than once, as charges settle and credits arrive. This page explains how data-finops keeps every publication, and which one it uses. The decisions are in ADR 0015, ADR 0019 and ADR 0020, with the calculation side in spec 03. They stay authoritative. To do it, see Handle a restated export. The whole Export Snapshot is the unit An Export Snapshot is every Billing Line of one Snapshot Scope (a billing account, a Billing Period and a source), as the provider published it at one time. A restatement replaces the whole Export Snapshot. data-finops never patches single Billing Lines, because a provider's restatement can change, add or remove any of them. Within an Export Snapshot, rows are never deduplicated. Two identical rows are two Billing Lines, each identified by its snapshot and position. A merge of these rows loses money that the provider billed. Then the totals of the Ledger are not equal to the totals of the provider. Stored Export Snapshots never change Each load has one of three outcomes: New: new content is stored. It is reported as new if it is now current, or as superseded if a later publication is current. Replay: content equal to the current Export Snapshot, or an ID already stored with the same content, stores nothing. Rejected: an ID already stored with different content is refused, because what was stored is never rewritten. The latest publication is current For each Snapshot Scope, the current Export Snapshot is the one the provider published last, with ties broken by the higher ID. It never depends on the order you load them in, so an earlier publication that arrives late cannot become current. The publication time comes only from the provider's own metadata. For an AWS Data Exports Delivery, that is the creation time in the manifest's data folder, never a file time or the load time. Earlier publications become Superseded Snapshots. They are kept as history. Allocations follow, and keep their history A Calculation Run allocates the current Export Snapshot of each Snapshot Scope. After a restatement, the next run makes a new Allocation Snapshot. The earlier one is kept, not overwritten. Its provenance shows that it is no longer current and which run superseded it. The API still serves it when you ask for it by its Calculation Run ID. Thus you can always explain a figure from last week as it was then. A Calculation Run whose inputs equal the current Allocation Snapshot's stores nothing. If the inputs are equal to the inputs of a superseded Allocation Snapshot, the run makes a new Allocation Snapshot. Thus a return to an earlier state is also recorded.

title: Security model
headings: Only the necessary metadata is kept
text: data-finops reads bills and workload metadata, which can show much about a business. This page explains how it limits who can reach it, what it accepts and what it keeps. The decisions are in ADR 0012 and ADR 0024. The threat model is in spec 05. Spec 04 tells what is kept, and spec 06 gives the errors of the API. These documents stay authoritative. Loopback by default By default, serve binds to 127.0.0.1. Then only the same machine can reach it, and a token is optional. It refuses to bind to a different address without a token. Only a literal loopback address counts: the system resolves a name such as localhost, and that name can point to any address. demo always serves on loopback with no token, so you can try data-finops without a secret. One bearer token If a token is configured, each route requires Authorization: Bearer <token>, also the dashboard and the API documentation. The HTTP transport of OpenLineage sends this header for its API key. A request with no token or with a wrong token gets 401. The comparison takes constant time. The token comes from DATA_FINOPS_TOKEN or a token file, never both. It must be at least 16 characters, without the spaces at its start and end. It is never logged, printed or stored. Errors say what is wrong with it, not what it is. It proves who has permission to send, not what a request is about: a token is never Evidence for an Identity Link. The token is for local and self-hosted use. A Deployment in AWS has no token. Its API accepts only IAM-signed requests. Producers write to an Inbox and do not send over HTTP. See Serve with a token and Deployment architecture. Bounded payloads One OpenLineage event can be 1 MiB at most. A larger body gets 413 at the cap, before it is read in full or parsed. A compressed body gets 415. Each event is sent uncompressed. Query history files, dbt artifacts and OpenLineage event files are capped at 512 MiB each. A larger file is rejected before it is read. Errors never echo input Every API error is an RFC 9457 Problem Details document. It names what was wrong, such as the field that failed validation, but never repeats the value sent. On the command line, a rejected item is named by its position and the reason, never by its content. A secret or a fragment of SQL in a bad input therefore never reaches a log or a terminal through an error. Only the necessary metadata is kept A Query Execution keeps only allowlisted metadata: identity, workgroup, statement type, catalog and database, state, times, error category and type, numeric statistics and engine version. Query text, execution parameters, state change reasons, error messages and unknown fields are dropped. From a Trusted Query Comment, only the dbt invocation and node are kept. Before an OpenLineage event is stored, the query text in its SQL facet and the stack traces in its error facets are removed. SQL quoted inside an error message is not detected. A rejected event is never stored. Query text is kept only after an explicit opt-in. No such opt-in exists today. No SQL literals or credentials are exported by the API or the dashboard. A Cost Explanation can show the Billing Line in full, tags and free-text names included, or only the columns the contract declares (ADR 0028). By default, serve shows the full line. With --explanation-detail minimal, it shows the minimal line. By default, a Deployment shows the minimal line. If its explanationDetail setting is full, it shows the full line. Anonymized samples The real-world sample in fixtures/reference-workload/ was anonymized before it was committed. Values were replaced with keyed pseudonyms, account IDs were replaced, and SQL was cut down. The scripts and their secret are described in Exit codes and environment.

title: Deployment architecture
text: A Deployment runs data-finops in one AWS account. It has no servers to operate and no network to manage. This page explains its parts, its trust boundaries and its cost. The decisions are in ADR 0026, ADR 0027 and ADR 0028. The design is in spec 08. These documents stay authoritative. Two functions and one bucket The right side of the diagram is the optional Public Demo, which the stack adds when publicDemo is true. The Public Demo explains it. This page is about the Deployment itself. data-finops keeps all its data in one SQLite file, and only one writer writes to it at a time. A Deployment keeps that design. It does not add a database server: The database is one S3 object, database/data-finops.sqlite, in the Deployment's private bucket. The collector is the only writer. One time each day, it downloads the object, runs one Collection Run and uploads the result. It uploads only if the object is still the object that it downloaded (an S3 conditional write on its ETag). If a different write occurs at the same time, the upload fails, so the other write is not lost. The next run starts again from the current object. The API only reads. It serves the object the last run wrote, never a half-written one, and downloads it again only when its ETag changes. Neither function runs in a VPC, so there is no NAT gateway, subnet or endpoint to pay for or secure. Both reach S3, Athena and CloudWatch through AWS's public endpoints, signed with their own roles. Pulled, not pushed Locally, OpenLineage events can arrive over HTTP with a bearer token. A Deployment has no such endpoint, for two reasons. The token is local to prevent one risk: a long-lived shared token on a public URL. Also, standard OpenLineage clients cannot sign requests for a URL that IAM authorizes. Thus producers write files to the Inbox, with an IAM policy that permits nothing else. The next Collection Run pulls the new files. Thus lineage arrives one time each day. That is also when data-finops calculates costs. See Send workload metadata to the Inbox. Trust boundaries The account. The FOCUS export, the Athena workgroups and the Deployment are in one account, and so are the IAM principals of its producers and readers. Nothing crosses into another account. The API Gateway HTTP API. It is reachable from the internet. But before the function runs, AWS rejects a request that is not signed. It also rejects a request if the signer does not have permission to invoke the route. A principal with the reader policy has this permission. Each route is a read under /v1/, so there is no write route to reach. Producers. A producer can put objects in the Inbox and do nothing else: not read them back, list them or touch the database. What it writes is screened like any input: each event capped at 1 MiB, each file at 512 MiB, and a rejected file reported by its key and reason, never its content. The collector's reach. It reads the export, the Athena history of the configured workgroups and the Inbox, and writes only the database object. It cannot run queries or read their results, which an explicit deny enforces. Query text is dropped before anything is stored. The bucket. The bucket blocks public access and disables ACLs. It denies requests without TLS. It encrypts objects with an S3-managed key or, as an option, with a customer-managed KMS key. S3 Versioning keeps earlier databases for noncurrentVersionDays. What readers see. By default, a Cost Explanation shows the minimal Billing Line, without tags and free-text names. The reason is that the readers of a Deployment can be a larger group than its billing administrators. The policy pack checks these rules on every pull request. Each function's role is limited to the actions that its job requires, and the pack fails a role granted anything more. The local rules are in Security model. What it costs The expected scale is a few thousand to about a million Billing Lines a month. At this scale, a Deployment costs less than $1 a month in us-east-1 while the Lambda free tier covers it. These numbers are estimates from the published AWS prices, checked on 2026-11-06. They are not measurements: Part Small About 1M lines a month Lambda, both functions (inside the free tier) $0.00 $0.00 S3 storage and requests about $0.01 about $0.29 CloudWatch Logs $0.00 to $0.05 $0.03 to $0.53 API Gateway HTTP API, at $1.00 for each million requests about $0.01 about $0.01 EventBridge Scheduler, the Budget $0.00 $0.00 Total about $0.02 to $0.07 about $0.33 to $0.83 The estimates assume a daily collector run of 60 seconds (small) to 300 seconds, with the default 2,048 MB of memory of the collector. They also assume 10,000 API requests a month, each of 1 second at 1 GB, and a database of 0.1 GB to 12 GB. Without Lambda's free tier, add about $0.18 (small) or $0.37 a month, which takes the larger case to about $1.20. A customer-managed KMS key adds $1 a month. AWS has no hard limit on spend, and a Budget cannot stop a function. Thus a Deployment limits its cost in these ways: Each function has a timeout and a memory size. The schedule runs one time each day, and a failed run gets two retries at most. Logs expire. Inbox objects and old database versions also expire. The optional Budget sends an email about forecast spend and actual spend. If a problem still occurs, you can stop the API at once. See Read a Deployment. Limits to watch Each Collection Run moves the whole database in and out of S3. As it grows, so do the run's time and the API's cold start. The /tmp of each function that copies the database is the ephemeralStorageMb setting, 10,240 MB by default. Lambda permits up to 10,240 MB. The database and the Inbox file that a run collects must fit in it. A database over 5 GB is refused when a function downloads it, because one upload to S3 holds 5 GB at most. Multipart upload is a revisit trigger. Athena keeps query history for 45 days. If a Deployment stops collection for a longer time, it loses the history of that gap. The summary shows a warning when this can have occurred. None of these is measured on a large account yet. Each is a revisit trigger in ADR 0026 or spec 08.

title: The Public Demo
headings: What is simulated and what is real
A static snapshot, not a live API
text: The Public Demo shows the dashboard of a real Deployment, with data that is about one day old. Anyone can open it, without an account. This page explains what is simulated, what is real, what is public and how it stays fresh. The decisions are in ADR 0029 (the site), ADR 0030 (the workload) and ADR 0031 (Cost Dimensions). The design is in spec 09. These documents stay authoritative. Open the Public Demo: d1qumy1toc5b1v.cloudfront.net. It shows data only after the first Collection Run that finds the demo's charges in the bill. What is simulated and what is real Each banner of the demo says the same thing: "Simulated workload; real Athena charges, reconciled to the bill; data trails by about a day; amounts before credits". Simulated: the orchestrator. There is no Airflow and no dbt. A scheduled Lambda function, the Simulated Orchestrator, plays both. Four times each day, it runs the DAGs that are due: daily_orders one time each day, hourly_events at each start and weekly_finance on Mondays. Each DAG has tasks, and each dbt task runs two to five models. Some tasks fail one time and succeed on the second try, and sometimes a run fails completely. Simulated: the records. It writes OpenLineage events and dbt artifacts in the shapes that the Airflow OpenLineage provider, dbt-ol and dbt write. They are made from the real, anonymized records of the reference workload, and they go into the Inbox as a real producer puts them. Tests run them through the same readers as real input. Simulated: the data and the people. The dataset of orders, customers and events is generated. The teams and tenants are fictional. Real: the queries. Each model runs real SQL in a dedicated Athena workgroup, data-finops-demo. The first line of each query is the dbt-athena query comment, with the model's node_id, the run's invocation_id, and the team, tenant and DAG run. A failed model fails as in dbt: Athena fails its query. Real: the bill. Athena charges for the scans. The charges arrive in the account's FOCUS export. A Collection Run then splits each Billing Line exactly among the queries in its scope, as for any other workgroup. The Identity Links to the Model Executions and DAG runs come from the same Evidence as for real dbt. The demo thus shows how data-finops works on a real bill. It is not evidence that real Airflow and dbt write these shapes. That evidence is the reference workload (ADR 0021). What is public The Deployment collects the FOCUS export of the whole account. Only the demo's part of it is published: Only the Athena usage lines of the data-finops-demo workgroup, and what comes from them: their Allocations, Roll-ups, Cost Dimensions, lineage and Cost Explanations. A Snapshot Scope with none of these lines is not published. Credit lines have no workgroup, so they are not published. The amounts are before credits. Each 12-digit account ID becomes the example account, 123456789012. Each Cost Explanation is the minimal one (ADR 0028). A Cost Dimension marked sensitive is not published. Only the current and the previous Billing Periods are published. The rest of the owner's bill is never published. A static snapshot, not a live API A Deployment's API is private: IAM authorizes each request, and a browser cannot sign one. A public live API would put compute and the whole bill on the open internet. Thus the demo publishes files, and nothing public computes anything: The collector writes the database object after each Collection Run. S3 starts the publisher. It reads the database with the same read model as the API. It writes each answer that the dashboard can ask for as a JSON file, in the shape of the API. This set of files is a Demo Snapshot. The publisher writes each snapshot under a new prefix, then moves current.json to it. Thus a reader never sees half a snapshot. current.json moves only forward in time, so an older snapshot never replaces a newer one. CloudFront serves the dashboard's files and the snapshots from a private bucket. It redirects HTTP to HTTPS. The dashboard is the same dashboard that data-finops serve shows. On the demo, it reads the snapshot's files instead of the API. A view that the snapshot does not cover shows "not in the public demo". For example, a sensitive Cost Dimension, a Billing Period before the previous one, and a Workload Run that no published cost reaches are not published. Thus in the lineage of a DAG run, a task run that ran no charged query shows "not in the public demo". How fresh it is The collector runs one time each day. The demo is as fresh as its last run. AWS delivers the bill some hours after the usage. The newest queries are not published until their Billing Line arrives. Thus the demo trails by about a day. The banner shows when the snapshot was published, and the Calculation Run of the Billing Period that the dashboard shows. S3 deletes each snapshot after 30 days. If no snapshot is published for 30 days, the demo shows nothing. What it costs The target is about $3 a month or less. Athena costs about $1 to $2, because each query scans from less than 10 MB to some hundred MB. CloudFront, S3, Lambda, EventBridge and Glue stay in their free tiers at the traffic of a demo. A $10 Budget alert stays on. The real cost of one month is recorded when the demo has run for a month. To stop the demo, set publicDemo to false and run pulumi up. This removes the demo and its bucket. To stop only the queries, disable the schedule of the simulator. See Deploy to AWS.

title: Compared with AWS's cost tools
text: AWS has its own cost tools. This page compares data-finops with them, for the one question that data-finops answers. What did each query, dbt model and Airflow DAG run cost, reconciled to the bill? It also says where AWS is better. The method is in spec 09, and the facts about each AWS tool, with their sources, are in the research note (checked on 2026-11-07). The evaluation is not done yet. It starts when the Public Demo has run for 7 days (#232). Until then, this page gives the method and what the AWS documentation says. It does not give results. The questions Each tool gets the same questions, on the same 7 days of the Public Demo: What did a dbt model cost last week? What did an Airflow DAG run cost? Which queries drove the bill of a workgroup? How much of the Athena bill is explained, and with what Confidence? Does every allocated cent reconcile to the invoice? What did each team and each tenant cost, reconciled? The tools Cost Explorer, with Cost Categories and tags. The query history in the Athena console. The FOCUS export, queried with Athena SQL. Cloud Intelligence Dashboards, from their documentation only. They require QuickSight, which costs money each month. data-finops, through the Public Demo and its API. For each tool and question, the evaluation records what the tool can answer and at what granularity. It also records how the answer reconciles to the bill, and what the tool costs. What the documentation says From the AWS documentation, before the evaluation: The finest unit is the workgroup. Athena can tag workgroups, but not queries. Cost Explorer and the FOCUS export thus stop at the workgroup. A cost below the workgroup, for example for a dbt model, must be built from the bill and the query metadata. No AWS tool links cost to dbt or Airflow. The Athena console shows the bytes that each query scanned, but not its cost, and not a reconciliation to the bill. Athena keeps the query history for 45 days. data-finops goes further. It splits each Billing Line among the Query Executions in its scope, and rolls them up to Model Executions and Workload Runs through explicit Evidence. Each Allocation states its Confidence and Coverage. Each Billing Line reconciles exactly. The evaluation checks each of these statements on the demo. Where AWS is better Breadth. The AWS tools cover each service: S3, Glue, compute and more. data-finops covers only the cost of Athena queries that are charged by the data that they scan. Maturity. AWS has commitments and discounts (Savings Plans, Reserved Instances), forecasts, anomaly detection, budgets and multi-account views. data-finops has none of these. No build. The AWS tools are already in the account. If one workgroup for each team answers your question, Cost Explorer with workgroup tags can be sufficient. Neither data-finops nor AWS splits the cost of Athena provisioned capacity or Athena for Spark among queries. Results The table of results comes here after the 7-day evaluation. The owner reviews it before it is published.

title: Contribute to data-finops
text: This site is for people who run data-finops. The documents for people who build it live in the repository, where they stay authoritative: AGENTS.md: how development works, and the engineering rules. GLOSSARY.md: the domain language every page uses. Specifications: what each part of data-finops must do. Decision records: the architecture decisions and why they were made. Plan: the milestones and their exit criteria. Progress: how each milestone was verified. Research: standards, reuse decisions and reviews. Tasks live in GitHub Issues. To change this site, edit the page in site/, then run python -m scripts.site build and python -m scripts.site check. To run all the checks of the repository, use python -m scripts.gates. The README tells you how to prepare the environments. The tests of the dashboard's static mode also need Node. To check a page against the Simplified Technical English rules, run python -m scripts.ste_check site/contributing.html. The rules are in the simplified-technical-english skill. The pages in scripts/ste_converted.txt are a gate in CI.
